items.description: President Donald Trump said Monday it is "highly unlikely" he will extend the two-week ceasefire with Iran if no agreement is reached before it expires on Wednesday, warning that military strikes on bridges and power plants could follow and that the naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz will remain in place until a deal is signed.[1][2]

items.title: Iran signals possible return to US talks after initial rejection

featured_image.name: Failed U.S.-Iran negotiations in Pakistan raise questions ... - PBS

items.description: The prospect of a second round of US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad swung between collapse and cautious revival on Monday as Tehran initially rejected participation, only to signal later in the day that it was "positively reviewing" a return to the negotiating table, according to a senior Iranian official who spoke to Reuters. The diplomatic whiplash came just two days before a fragile ceasefire between the two sides is set to expire on Wednesday, April 22.[1][2][3]

items.title: White House says US ready to back UAE financially amid Iran war

featured_image.name: UAE asks US for a wartime financial lifeline | MEO

items.description:
White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett confirmed on Monday that the United States is prepared to provide financial assistance to the United Arab Emirates should the ongoing war with Iran further damage the Gulf state's economic outlook, though he indicated Washington does not expect such a step will be necessary.[1]

The remarks follow a report by The Wall Street Journal that UAE Central Bank Governor Khaled Mohamed Balama raised the prospect of establishing a currency-swap line with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and officials from the Federal Reserve during meetings in Washington last week. No formal request for a swap line has been submitted, and Emirati representatives framed the discussions as a "preliminary and precautionary measure".[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Trump to consider lifting Hormuz blockade after Pakistan army chief's call

featured_image.name: U.S. Seizes Iranian Cargo Ship Amid Peace Talk Standoff

items.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump told Pakistan's Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir in a phone call that he would consider his advice on lifting the Strait of Hormuz naval blockade, a Pakistani security source said on Monday, in a development that could open a path to resuming stalled peace talks with Iran as a ceasefire nears expiration.[1][2]

The exchange came as a U.S. delegation was set to travel to Islamabad on Monday for a second round of Pakistan-brokered negotiations, though Tehran has not confirmed whether it will attend.[3][4]

items.title: Fungus from NASA cleanrooms survived simulated Mars trip

featured_image.name: Fungi may survive extreme conditions of Mars and space, say ...

items.description:
A fungus found lurking in NASA's ultra-clean spacecraft assembly rooms could withstand the punishing conditions of a trip to Mars and persist on the planet's surface, according to new research that raises fresh questions about keeping other worlds free from Earth's biology.

The study, published this week in Applied and Environmental Microbiology, is the first to demonstrate that a microbial eukaryote — a complex, nucleus-bearing organism — could survive every phase of a Mars mission, from pre-launch preparation through space travel to robotic surface exploration.[1][2]

items.title: Iran pulls out of US talks after ship seizure

featured_image.name: Iran says no talks with US for now, casting doubt over Pakistan efforts

items.description:
The United States military fired on and seized an Iranian-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday, the first known use of force in Washington's naval blockade of Iranian ports, throwing a fragile ceasefire into crisis less than 48 hours before it is set to expire.

U.S. Central Command said the guided-missile destroyer USS Spruance intercepted the Touska, a 294-meter cargo vessel, as it sailed through the Arabian Sea toward the Iranian port of Bandar Abbas. After the crew ignored repeated warnings, the warship used its deck gun to disable the vessel's engine room, and Marines from the 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit boarded from helicopters launched off the amphibious assault ship USS Tripoli.[1][2][3]

President Donald Trump announced the seizure on Truth Social, writing that the ship had been "stopped right in its tracks by a hole in the engine room" and that Marines had taken control. The Touska and its owners were already under U.S. Treasury sanctions for allegedly helping Iran evade trade restrictions.[2][1]

items.title: UAE warns it may settle oil trades in yuan without US dollar backstop

featured_image.name: UAE Discusses Potential Dollar Swap Line With US, WSJ ...

items.description: The United Arab Emirates has warned the United States that it may begin settling oil and gas transactions in Chinese yuan if Washington fails to provide a dollar liquidity backstop, according to the Wall Street Journal. The threat marks a striking fracture in the petrodollar system at a moment when the ongoing war between the US and Iran has strained Gulf economies and called into question American security commitments in the region.[1][2]

items.title: Eni announces giant gas discovery offshore Indonesia

featured_image.name: Indonesia Gas Discovery at Konta-1 Dir Well in Kutai Basin ...

items.description:
Eni announced on Monday a giant gas discovery at the Geliga-1 exploration well in the Ganal block of the Kutei Basin, offshore Indonesia, with preliminary estimates pointing to in-place resources of approximately 5 trillion cubic feet of gas and 300 million barrels of condensate.[1][2]

The find adds to a string of deepwater successes for the Italian energy company in Southeast Asia and could pave the way for a third production hub in one of Indonesia's most prolific offshore basins.
